title: N+1 rescue with a query counter
prompt: Implement fetch_user_orders using at most 2 db.query calls total; per-user order lists preserve db row order; empty user_ids returns {} with zero queries.

tests.name: two queries, all users, ordered rows
tests.code:
class DB:
    def __init__(self):
        self.queries = 0
    def query(self, sql, params):
        self.queries += 1
        rows = [(1, 11, 5.0), (2, 21, 7.5), (1, 12, 3.0), (3, 31, 9.9), (2, 22, 1.0)]
        ids = set(params[0])
        return [r for r in rows if r[0] in ids]

db = DB()
out = fetch_user_orders([1, 2, 3], db)
assert db.queries <= 2, f'queries: {db.queries}'
assert out[1] == [{'id': 11, 'total': 5.0}, {'id': 12, 'total': 3.0}], f'out[1]: {out[1]}'
assert out[2] == [{'id': 21, 'total': 7.5}, {'id': 22, 'total': 1.0}]
assert out[3] == [{'id': 31, 'total': 9.9}]
print('ok')
tests.hint: One query with all ids (IN-clapse style via the db helper) and group rows by user_id in Python.

tests.name: empty input makes zero queries
tests.hint: Guard the empty case before any query.
